patternsRaw.name: powershell-command-separator-syntax
patternsRaw.observation: The agent repeatedly used `&&` to chain commands in `exec` tool calls, which resulted in a PowerShell `ParserError` because PowerShell requires `;` for command separation in this context. The agent successfully resolved the issue by replacing `&&` with `;` or using separate `exec` calls.
patternsRaw.guidance: When using the `exec` tool with PowerShell on Windows, use `;` instead of `&&` to chain commands, or issue separate `exec` calls for each command to avoid parser errors.

patternsRaw.name: python-and-unix-utilities-unavailable
patternsRaw.observation: The agent attempted to start an HTTP server using Python commands and use Unix utilities like `head`, but all failed with command not found errors in the PowerShell environment. The agent successfully started a server using Node.js built-in modules and verified the HTTP response using the PowerShell cmdlet `Invoke-WebRequest`.
patternsRaw.guidance: When Python or common Unix CLI utilities are unavailable in the PowerShell environment, use Node.js built-in modules to create servers or perform HTTP requests, and use PowerShell cmdlets like `Invoke-WebRequest` or `Get-Content` instead of Unix commands.

skillsRaw.name: powershell-command-separator-syntax
skillsRaw.description: Use when chaining commands in the `exec` tool with PowerShell on Windows to avoid parser errors caused by using `&&`.
skillsRaw.instructions:
1. Identify any command chaining in `exec` tool calls that uses the `&&` operator.
2. Replace the `&&` operator with a semicolon `;` to separate commands within the same `exec` call.
3. Alternatively, issue separate `exec` calls for each individual command instead of chaining them.
skillsRaw.applicability: Applicable whenever the `exec` tool uses PowerShell as the shell on a Windows machine.

skillsRaw.name: nodejs-and-powershell-alternatives-for-unix-tools
skillsRaw.description: Use when Python or common Unix CLI utilities are unavailable in the PowerShell environment and you need to start servers or perform HTTP requests and file operations.
skillsRaw.instructions:
1. When Python commands or Unix utilities fail with command not found errors in the PowerShell environment, switch to Node.js or PowerShell built-in alternatives.
2. Use Node.js built-in modules via inline Node.js execution to create local HTTP servers or perform necessary file and network operations.
3. Use PowerShell cmdlets like `Invoke-WebRequest` or `Get-Content` to verify HTTP responses or read file contents instead of using Unix commands.
skillsRaw.applicability: Applicable when working in a PowerShell environment on Windows where Python and standard Unix CLI utilities are not available.

# Pattern 1
## Name
powershell-command-separator-syntax
## Observation
The agent repeatedly used `&&` to chain commands in `exec` tool calls, which resulted in a PowerShell `ParserError` because PowerShell requires `;` for command separation in this context. The agent successfully resolved the issue by replacing `&&` with `;` or using separate `exec` calls.
## Guidance
When using the `exec` tool with PowerShell on Windows, use `;` instead of `&&` to chain commands, or issue separate `exec` calls for each command to avoid parser errors.

# Pattern 2
## Name
python-and-unix-utilities-unavailable

The agent attempted to start an HTTP server using Python commands and use Unix utilities like `head`, but all failed with command not found errors in the PowerShell environment. The agent successfully started a server using Node.js built-in modules and verified the HTTP response using the PowerShell cmdlet `Invoke-WebRequest`.
## Guidance
When Python or common Unix CLI utilities are unavailable in the PowerShell environment, use Node.js built-in modules to create servers or perform HTTP requests, and use PowerShell cmdlets like `Invoke-WebRequest` or `Get-Content` instead of Unix commands.

# Skill 1
## Name
powershell-command-separator-syntax
## Description
Use when chaining commands in the `exec` tool with PowerShell on Windows to avoid parser errors caused by using `&&`.
## Instructions
1. Identify any command chaining in `exec` tool calls that uses the `&&` operator.
2. Replace the `&&` operator with a semicolon `;` to separate commands within the same `exec` call.
3. Alternatively, issue separate `exec` calls for each individual command instead of chaining them.
## Applicability
Applicable whenever the `exec` tool uses PowerShell as the shell on a Windows machine.

# Skill 2
## Name
nodejs-and-powershell-alternatives-for-unix-tools
## Description
Use when Python or common Unix CLI utilities are unavailable in the PowerShell environment and you need to start servers or perform HTTP requests and file operations.
## Instructions
1. When Python commands or Unix utilities fail with command not found errors in the PowerShell environment, switch to Node.js or PowerShell built-in alternatives.
2. Use Node.js built-in modules via inline Node.js execution to create local HTTP servers or perform necessary file and network operations.
3. Use PowerShell cmdlets like `Invoke-WebRequest` or `Get-Content` to verify HTTP responses or read file contents instead of using Unix commands.
## Applicability
Applicable when working in a PowerShell environment on Windows where Python and standard Unix CLI utilities are not available.
